title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G is a connected pro-algebraic group over Q, the 'motivic Galois group' of a 'situation motivique' (a Tannakian category M with weights). epsilon: G -> G_m is the Tate or weight character, the action on Q(1). U = Ker(G° -> G_m). The line 'G_m ... un élément central' together with the later 'existence de g avec epsilon g(lambda) = lambda^2' shows there is a central weight cocharacter g: G_m -> G with epsilon∘g = [2]. This is exactly the data that Saavedra (1972) and Deligne–Milne (1982, §5) later formalized as a Tate triple (M, w, T(1)). G_R is the gerbe, or torsor, of R-valued fibre functors, presumably 'normalised' ones compatible with the weight/Tate structure.

Proposition 1 (equivalent conditions):
(i) U contains a torus (reading uncertain).
(ii) epsilon is 'positive', i.e. not a square, among the normalised characters G -> G_m.
(iii) M_R has a fibre functor, i.e. G_R is non-empty.
(iv) M has only even degrees (weights), i.e. g(mu_2) = 1, written '= 0'.

Proposition 2 is the complementary case:
(i) U = U° x mu_2.
(ii) epsilon admits a normalised square root, a 'half Tate twist'.
(iii) G_R is empty.

Sketch of proof:
- (i) <=> (ii) follows formally from the existence of g with epsilon∘g = lambda^2.
- (iii) => (ii): in a polarised category, the objects of odd degree have even rank, because a 'forme hermitienne fondamentale' (polarisation) is alternating in odd weight. This is the standard argument that odd-weight H^1 carries a symplectic form.
- (i) => (iii): the obstruction to an R-fibre functor lies in an H^1(R, T) for a torus T, which Grothendieck asserts is 0.
- Even weights => (iii): if g(mu_2) is trivial, then g = 2g' with epsilon∘g' = id. This splits the weight structure and gives an R-fibre functor.
- Corollary: for arbitrary M, the even-weight motivic subcategory M^pair, with group G/g(mu_2), admits an R-fibre functor.

Margin notes. The ink note says only axioms 1, 2, 3 of a 'situation motivique' are used. The pencil note suggests replacing the motivic situation by a category of (polarised) forms characterised by a fibre functor.

Purpose. This is the real-place analysis of the Galois theory of motives: when is the motivic category over R neutral? It identifies the obstruction with the sign/weight cocharacter and the parity of weights. It anticipates Saavedra Ch. VI (polarisations) and Deligne–Milne §5 (Tate triples over R; the even-weight part is neutral over R).
errors: The justification of (i) => (iii) via 'si T est un tore [compact?] sur R, H^1(R,T)=0' is false as read. H^1(R,T)=0 holds for split tori (Hilbert 90) and induced tori R_{C/R}G_m. For the compact torus U(1) one gets H^1(R,U(1)) = R^*/R_{>0} = Z/2, and for an anisotropic torus of dimension n, H^1(R,T) = (Z/2)^n. Either the adjective is 'déployé' (in which case the step is fine), or the argument has a gap.

The equivalences between the numbered conditions are sketchy. In Prop 1 it is unclear whether (i) reads 'U a un tore' or 'U n'a pas de ...'. The dichotomy Prop 1 / Prop 2 only works if exactly one of 'epsilon has a normalised square root' / 'not' holds, which needs connectedness hypotheses; these are only implicit.
'g(mu_2) = 0' should read g(mu_2) = 1 (trivial); this is notational.

ideas.what: Weight cocharacter g: G_m -> G, central, with epsilon∘g = squaring; the motivic Galois group with the Tate character as structure
ideas.modern_name: Tate triple (weight grading w plus Tate object T(1) with w acting by -2)
ideas.where_published: Saavedra, Catégories tannakiennes, LNM 265; Deligne–Milne, LNM 900

ideas.what: Existence of an R-fibre functor (neutrality over R) for a motivic category, characterised by parity of weights / existence of a square root of the Tate character
ideas.modern_name: Fibre functors over R for Tate triples; the even-weight subcategory is neutral over R

ideas.what: Odd-weight objects have even rank because of a fundamental (alternating) hermitian form
ideas.modern_name: Polarisation / symplectic pairing on odd weight
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Hodge theory); Saavedra/Deligne for Tannakian polarisations

ideas.what: Half Tate twist: whether epsilon admits a 'normalised' square root
ideas.modern_name: Existence of Q(1/2) / square root of the Tate motive

missed.claim: This is an early Grothendieck draft of the real-place analysis of motivic Galois groups: the dichotomy that G_R is empty or not according to whether the Tate character has a normalised square root, and neutrality of M^pair over R. In the literature this is attributed to Saavedra (his student) and Deligne–Milne. The page documents Grothendieck's own priority on the formulation, though the ideas themselves are known.
missed.quote: Cor Si M est quelconque, la sous-catégorie motivique M^pair ... admet un R-foncteur fibre.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution of the Tate-triple / real-neutrality results; it shows these were part of the 1965-ish 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' programme.

deep.surprise_reason: Content matches results later published by Saavedra and Deligne–Milne (Tate triples over R, even-weight part neutral). It is of interest as evidence of Grothendieck's own early formulation, not as new mathematics. It also contains a dubious H^1 claim for compact tori.
transcription_corrections: 'g(mu_2) = 0' should be understood as g(mu_2) trivial.
The word before 'sur R' in 'si T est un tore ... sur R' is uncertain; it could be 'déployé' rather than 'compact', which matters for correctness.
'J = 2J'' and 'epsilon J' = id' likely refer to the weight cocharacter (the same as g), possibly 'g = 2g''.
Prop 2 (i): 'U° un tore dans Ker(G°, G_m)' is uncertain.
